mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over a three-month window signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 1 million units signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < 1000 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero during such episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a shift from spending to saving, which typically precedes a slowdown in economic growth and negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases AND GDPC1 decreases for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid reduction in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recession signals an aggressive monetary easing, which supports risk assets and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in more than 70% of such episodes (t-test p > 0.01).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, boosting consumer spending and corporate profits, and thus positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated increase in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 2% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals a broad-based supply-side recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 2% AND HOUST > 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in more than 50% of triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).
